Question: Is the “ability to consummate” concept subject to Material Adverse Effect (MAE) carveouts?

"Section 7.4 – Definition of Adverse Impact: "Adverse Impact" means any event, change, or series of events that, either individually or in aggregate, would impair or materially delay the consummation of the Transaction.    (ii) Delays in consummation caused exclusively by currency exchange volatility, minor adjustments to GAAP, or errors in public disclosure related to the Agreement shall be excluded from the definition of Adverse Impact.
   (iii) In no event shall an adverse effect that is directly attributed to these specified exceptions, including any resultant delay in achieving consummation, be taken into account when assessing a Material Adverse Effect.
Moreover, while the definition of Adverse Impact broadly covers factors affecting the Transaction, it expressly carves out and excludes any purely temporal delays in consummation that arise from the circumstances listed in clauses (i) and (ii). Thus, any such effect on the ability to consummate is subject to the MAE carveout regime herein established."

End of Agreement.
